findings.issue_text: [BUG] ENV_FILE is hardcoded to the relative path "../.env", which only resolves to the repo-root .env when the script is invoked with scripts/ as the working directory. A developer runs `bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root (the standard way to invoke a script in scripts/); `../.env` then resolves outside the repository, so the script touches/creates a .env in the parent directory and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never written to the real .env — the dev server keeps registering Google webhooks against the stale or missing URL and the script reports success ("✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in ../.env").

[BUG] SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is called with an empty Prisma update payload, and the diff adds no explicit write of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (the only schema change is on CalendarCache), so no field of SelectedCalendar is ever written. The core mechanism of the feature fails: Prisma's updateMany with an empty data object raises a PrismaClientValidationError on the availability-refresh path (crashing fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache after the cache write), or at best performs a no-op leaving SelectedCalendar.updatedAt unchanged — either way the 'Last updated' timestamp shown in CredentialActionsDropdown never reflects the refresh the call was added to signal.

[BUG] The new call references SelectedCalendarRepository but the diff contains no import for it in CalendarService.ts (no hunk touches the file's import block), so the module resolves an undefined identifier unless the base file already imported it. If the import is absent in the base file, the first availability refresh for any Google credential throws `ReferenceError: SelectedCalendarRepository is not defined`, turning every cache-refresh cycle into a 500 and breaking calendar sync — a missing prerequisite the diff never establishes.

[ADVISORY] The dev:cron script now depends on tsx via `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but the diff adds no tsx dependency to apps/web/package.json, so tsx is resolved from the npm registry at run time instead of the lockfile. Running `yarn dev:cron` offline (or in CI with a network-restricted environment) fails with an npx fetch error, and when it does fetch, it pins nothing — the cron-tester toolchain is non-reproducible; replacing ts-node without adding tsx to devDependencies is the missing-tool half of the migration.

[ADVISORY] The script invokes `tmole` without checking it exists on PATH or documenting how to install it. A developer without tunnelmole installed runs the script: `tmole $TM_PORT > "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &` writes 'command not found' into the log, the 20-iteration grep loop silently burns 10 seconds, and the user gets the misleading '❌ Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL.' with no hint that the missing tool is the cause.

[ADVISORY] In the reuse branch, TUNNEL_URL is extracted from /tmp/tmole.log, which need not exist or contain a URL for an already-running tmole started by a different session or after a reboot. When tmole is genuinely running and reusable but the log file was cleaned (`rm -f` only runs in the start branch) or was never written by that process, extract_url_from_log returns empty, the script declares '❌ Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL' and exits even though the tunnel is live and only the log is missing — the reuse fast-path fails in exactly the scenarios it exists for.

[ADVISORY] The handler instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository directly, bypassing whatever selection point swaps in CalendarCacheRepositoryMock when calendar-cache is disabled (the mock's own log message, 'Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled', documents that selection exists). When the calendar-cache feature is disabled, every connectedCalendars fetch still issues a calendarCache.groupBy query against the database, adding an unconditional DB round-trip to a hot settings-page endpoint that the feature flag is supposed to make inert.

[ADVISORY] The handler throws a plain Error('Credential not found or access denied') instead of a TRPCError (NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN). Both the not-found case and the ownership-violation case surface to the client as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) with a raw message, so the UI's onError toast reports 'Error deleting cache' for what is a normal authorization failure and server-side error tracking is polluted with expected 4xx-class events logged as 5xx.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds non-trivial new server logic — the deleteCache mutation (ownership check + deleteMany) and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds (groupBy/_max aggregation) — with no test anywhere in the diff, while the existing calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts had to be manually extended to keep implementing the interface. A regression in the ownership check (e.g. dropping the userId filter) or in the groupBy aggregation ships silently; the parallel hand-maintained interface/mock/implementation triple now has a fourth method that only the mock's copy can drift on.

[BUG] deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error('Credential not found or access denied') when the credential is missing or owned by another user, which tRPC surfaces as a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a 4xx NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN. A user whose dropdown references a credential that was deleted in another tab (or any client sending an arbitrary credentialId) gets a generic server-error toast via the component's onError path, and ops gets 5xx noise for what is a normal client-error case; the contract for this mutation has no defined 4xx error shape.

[BUG] connectedCalendars.handler.ts instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly and deleteCache.handler.ts calls prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly, bypassing the disabled-feature repository path that calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts exists to serve ('Skipping getCacheStatusByCredentialIds due to calendar-cache being disabled'). When the calendar-cache feature is disabled, the connectedCalendars query still hits the calendarCache table and returns real updatedAt values, so the UI renders the 'Cache Status' dropdown with a working delete action for a feature that is turned off — the exact state the mock was built to prevent.

[ADVISORY] The new non-trivial logic in this diff — deleteCacheHandler's ownership check plus deletion, CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds (groupBy/_max), SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId, and CredentialActionsDropdown's conditional rendering and mutation wiring — has no test anywhere in the diff (the only test-shaped addition is scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh, a bash dev-tunnel utility, not a test suite). A regression in the ownership check (e.g., dropping the userId filter) or in the groupBy-based status mapping would ship silently; the ownership check is security-adjacent and is currently verified by nothing.

[ADVISORY] The new `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` executes unconditionally on every invocation of the availability fetch path, including every cache-hit that served from cache without any refresh. Every availability/booking-slot computation for Google Calendar now performs an extra UPDATE across all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential — multiplied across every page load that checks availability, this turns a read-mostly hot path into a write-heavy one and fires needless row writes (and @updatedAt churn) with no cache activity to justify them.

[ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` locale instead of the user's locale from useLocale(). Every non-en-US user sees the 'Last updated' timestamp in US date format (MM/DD/YYYY, 12-hour) regardless of their app language — inconsistent with every other locale-aware date render in the surrounding settings UI.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` to the allSelectedCalendars/userLevelSelectedCalendars selects and adds the updateManyByCredentialId bump in CalendarService, but nothing in the diff consumes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt — the UI's cache status is sourced from CalendarCache.updatedAt via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds instead. Two parallel 'cache freshness' mechanisms are now maintained (SelectedCalendar.updatedAt written on every fetch, CalendarCache.updatedAt displayed in the UI) with only the latter read anywhere in this diff; the extra DB writes and selection columns are unverifiable as needed, and the next reader may reasonably assume the two timestamps agree when they measure different events (per-calendar bump vs per-cache-row write).

[ADVISORY] getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores the expiresAt column, so the 'Last updated: <timestamp>' status is computed from cache rows that may already be expired and will never be refreshed until the next availability fetch. A user whose cache expired hours or days ago sees a fresh-looking 'Last updated' timestamp implying their availability data is current, when the served availability either misses the cache or comes from a stale source; the status the feature advertises is not the status of the data actually served.

[ADVISORY] A new 79-line Tunnelmole webhook-testing developer script is included in a PR whose stated intent is 'add calendar cache status and actions' — this work is not traceable to any requirement in the PR. Reviewers and operators of this feature must review, maintain, and carry a macOS-only (BSD `sed -i ''` syntax fails on GNU sed) tunnel-management script forever under a feature PR; unrelated tooling changes ride in without their own review context, and the script mutates the developer's `../.env` as a side effect.

[ADVISORY] The `dev:cron` script change from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` is unrelated tooling drift inside a calendar-cache feature PR. Anyone bisecting cron-tester failures must now wade through this feature PR; the change also silently switches the runner from ts-node to tsx, altering module-resolution/transpilation behavior for cron-tester with no requirement justifying it.

[ADVISORY] The new unconditional `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` write in the availability-fetch path is not traceable to any requirement: nothing in this diff reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (the UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds instead). Every availability fetch — including the cache-hit path, since the write sits after the cache-refresh block and runs on every call — performs a DB write affecting all SelectedCalendars under the credential, during the hot booking-availability path, to maintain a timestamp no code consumes; this is pure write amplification plus dead work.

[ADVISORY] `updateManyByCredentialId` accepts a fully generic `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` parameter whose only call site in the entire diff passes `{}` — speculative generality with no consumer of the generality. The repository surface grows a mutable-data API that exists only to be called with empty data; the next change touching SelectedCalendar writes now has two overlapping update entry points (updateById, updateWhere, updateManyByCredentialId) to reason about, and the empty-data idiom's actual effect (bumping @updatedAt) is implicit and undocumented at the call site.

[ADVISORY] The `UserWithCalendars` type is widened with `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` fields that no code in this diff consumes. Dead API-surface expansion: every consumer of this shared type now carries two fields with no reader, and future readers cannot tell whether the fields are contractual (they appear in a public type) or vestigial from this PR.

[ADVISORY] The UserRepository `allSelectedCalendars` select adds `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` that nothing in this diff reads, matching the dead widening in getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts. A widely-used user-fetch query is broadened for fields with no consumer in this PR, coupling a hot user-query's select list to speculative needs and forcing every future consumer of this query to transfer the extra columns.

[BUG] The 'Credential not found or access denied' path throws a bare `Error`, which tRPC surfaces to the client as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) instead of a 4xx (NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN). A user whose credentialId belongs to another user (or was concurrently deleted) gets a 500 that pages error monitors as a server fault, when it is an ordinary authorization failure the client should treat as a 4xx; the dropdown's `onError` toast also shows a generic error for what is a benign denial.

[ADVISORY] The new handler bypasses the `ICalendarCacheRepository` abstraction entirely, calling `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly even though the same PR extends that interface and its disabled-feature mock with `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` — the interface already has a `deleteManyByCredential` member. Two parallel paths now exist for cache deletion (repository method vs raw prisma in the handler); when cache deletion behavior changes (e.g., the disabled-feature mock needs to suppress deletes, or soft-delete is added), the mock's 'Skipping deleteManyByCredential due to calendar-cache being disabled' path will not cover this handler, producing divergent behavior between environments with cache disabled.

[BUG] The handler instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly, bypassing the disabled-feature mock selection mechanism that this same PR's `calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts` exists for (its log message 'Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled' implies a runtime swap elsewhere). When the calendar-cache feature is disabled, the connectedCalendars query still executes a `groupBy` against the CalendarCache table on every fetch; the interface's disabled-path contract is silently not honored for this new method, so the status field is computed via real DB reads in configurations where every other calendar-cache operation is a no-op.

[ADVISORY] The disconnect half of this new component duplicates DisconnectIntegration's flow (credential delete mutation, success/error toasts, confirmation dialog, post-settle invalidations) as a parallel hand-maintained copy rather than reusing or extending the existing component. The two disconnect implementations will drift: any future fix to DisconnectIntegration (different invalidations, error handling, confirm copy) will not reach this dropdown (or vice versa), and users get different disconnect behavior depending on which surface they are on.

[BUG] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` while the component uses `useLocale()` for all other strings, so the date renders in US format for every locale. Non-English users see 'Last updated' with en-US date/time ordering (MM/DD, 12-hour clock) inconsistent with their locale — a visible i18n regression introduced alongside i18n string additions in the same PR.

[ADVISORY] The only consumer wired to the new `cacheUpdatedAt` field and `CredentialActionsDropdown` in this diff is the platform atoms wrapper; no core settings surface in the diff renders the cache status or delete action, so the feature's visibility is scoped to one (platform/embed) surface only. Users managing calendars in the standard web-app settings path get none of the shipped cache status/delete behavior, while the backend (deleteCache mutation, cache-status query, CalendarCache.updatedAt migration) is fully shipped for everyone — a half-wired feature whose remaining wiring is invisible to this PR's reviewers.

[ADVISORY] The `findMany` refactor drops the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` compile-time check, an unrelated change in a calendar-cache PR that removes type validation of the `where`/`select`/`orderBy` shape. Future callers passing a malformed select or where clause that previously failed the build at this repository boundary now type-check and fail only at runtime; the change has no traceable connection to the cache-status feature to justify the lost safety.

[BUG] The new 'touch' write updates SelectedCalendar.updatedAt via SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId, but the cache status surfaced to users (connectedCalendars.handler -> getCacheStatusByCredentialIds) reads CalendarCache.updatedAt — the writer and the reader target two different tables with the same conceptual meaning. SelectedCalendar.updatedAt becomes a phantom-maintained field: the explicit write after every availability fetch updates a column that no code in this diff reads, while the 'Cache Status: Last updated' shown in the dropdown reflects only CalendarCache row upserts. If the intent was that the touch mark calendars as refreshed, that signal never reaches the UI; if the intent was the CalendarCache timestamp, the write in CalendarService (and the new updateManyByCredentialId repository method, plus the updatedAt/googleChannelId fields added to the SelectedCalendar selects) is dead code that still costs an UPDATE on every cache fill for every calendar row under the credential.

[BUG] deleteCacheHandler authorizes via prisma.credential.findFirst({ id, userId: user.id }), which cannot match delegation credentials (userId is null for org-owned/delegation credentials), yet the UI explicitly renders the 'Delete cached data' action for calendars carrying a delegationCredentialId. A user whose Google Calendar connection is backed by a delegation credential sees 'Delete cached data' in CredentialActionsDropdown (canDisconnect is false but hasCache can be true), clicks it, and every attempt fails: findFirst returns null, the handler throws 'Credential not found or access denied', and the user gets the generic 'Error deleting cache' toast — the feature is permanently broken for the delegation path the same diff chose to support in the UI.

[ADVISORY] The handler bypasses the calendar-cache repository layer entirely, calling prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly even though ICalendarCacheRepository already declares deleteManyByCredential (visible in calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts and its mock). Two parallel data-access paths now own CalendarCache mutations: repository-backed paths (upsert/delete via the interface) and a raw-prisma path in the tRPC router. The mock's 'calendar-cache disabled' behavior is skipped for this operation, and any future change to cache deletion semantics (e.g., also touching related rows, honoring the feature flag) must be made in two places — the next change gets riskier because the ownership boundary was not used.

[ADVISORY] The handler hard-instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository instead of resolving it through the existing disabled-mode mechanism, so getCacheStatusByCredentialIds on the CalendarCacheRepositoryMock is unreachable in the real wiring and the groupBy query runs unconditionally. Deployments where the calendar-cache feature is disabled still pay a CalendarCache groupBy on every connectedCalendars fetch (a settings-page hot path), and the mock's new method exists only to satisfy the interface — the disabled mode this codebase models explicitly is contradicted by this call site.

[ADVISORY] deleteCacheMutation has no cache invalidation of its own (unlike disconnectMutation, which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars in onSettled), so the displayed cacheUpdatedAt only refreshes if every caller's onSuccess happens to refetch. After a successful 'Delete cached data', the dropdown continues to show the old 'Last updated: <timestamp>' from the cached connectedCalendars response; users see a stale cache status that contradicts the deletion they just performed, unless each future consumer of this component remembers to wire onSuccess to a refetch.

[BUG] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) locale instead of the user's locale, inside a component that otherwise routes all copy through useLocale(). Every non-en-US user sees US-format dates/times (MM/DD/YYYY, 12-hour clock) for the cache status, inconsistent with the rest of the localized settings UI — a format drift between the app's locale pipeline and this one rendering site.

[ADVISORY] The findMany refactor drops the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` compile-time conformance check while changing the method's behavior in the same diff. Callers can now pass a `select`/`where`/`orderBy` shape that does not conform to Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs with no compile error; the type guard that previously caught drift between the repository contract and Prisma's input type is gone, so the next change to this method loses that safety net silently.

[ADVISORY] updatedAt and googleChannelId are newly added to the SelectedCalendar select on the hot user-fetch path, but no code in this diff consumes either field (the displayed status comes from CalendarCache, and googleChannelId has no reader here). Every user load that fetches these relations ships two additional columns that nothing reads; the fields are inert payload added to a shared query shape, and the next reader cannot tell whether they are load-bearing or removable — the change-safety of this query degrades.

[ADVISORY] The new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groupBy filters and groups CalendarCache by credentialId, but the diff adds no index on CalendarCache.credentialId to serve it. connectedCalendars (a frequently-hit settings/onboarding path) now issues a groupBy over CalendarCache — a table holding free/busy JSON payloads that grows with every cached window — and without a matching index each call degrades to a scan of that table as cache rows accumulate.

[ADVISORY] The added `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` call bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt on every availability fetch, but the feature's cache-status UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt (via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds in connectedCalendars.handler.ts), not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt — a remnant of an earlier design iteration in which cache freshness was tracked per SelectedCalendar. Every calendar availability fetch performs an unconditional UPDATE across all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential that nothing in this diff consumes (UserRepository now selects updatedAt/googleChannelId but no rendering or logic uses them); if any out-of-diff consumer relies on SelectedCalendar.updatedAt semantics (e.g. channel-expiry logic keyed off last-touch time), bumping it on every busy-slot fetch silently corrupts that behavior.

[ADVISORY] The `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` fields added to the selectedCalendars select are dead weight in this diff — the connectedCalendars handler derives cacheUpdatedAt from the CalendarCache table, so no consumer reads these newly fetched columns. Rows are fetched and shipped to the client on every connectedCalendars query carrying data nothing renders; the next reader of this code assumes these fields drive the cache-status UI and wastes time tracing a data path that does not exist.

[ADVISORY] The UserWithCalendars type is widened to include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on both calendar arrays, but the only diff consumer of connectedCalendars (connectedCalendars.handler.ts) attaches `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache instead — the type contract was changed for a design that was subsequently abandoned mid-iteration. The public type now promises fields that carry no feature behavior; every future implementer of UserWithCalendars must populate two columns for a feature that reads a different table, and the mismatch between the type and the actual data flow is discovered only at review time, not compile time.

[ADVISORY] The `dev:cron` script was silently swapped from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` inside a feature PR about calendar cache status — an unrelated change to the developer toolchain that no review iteration explicitly accepted as part of the objective. The stated PR intent (cache status and actions) no longer matches the diff contents: bisecting, reverting, or cherry-picking the cache feature drags a dev-runner change along, and a reviewer approving 'cache status' is unknowingly approving a Node runner migration (different tsconfig/ESM behavior) with no mention in the PR description.

[ADVISORY] A brand-new Tunnelmole webhook-testing script is bundled into a calendar-cache-status PR with no connection to the feature, and `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the caller's CWD, not the script's location. Running the script as `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root makes `../.env` resolve to a file outside the repository: the script reports '✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL' while writing to the wrong file and the app never receives the tunnel URL — a silent success on a broken path. Additionally, this tooling change rides into the cache-status PR unaccepted, so reverting the feature or bisecting webhook issues entangles this script.

[ADVISORY] The new component silently replaces DisconnectIntegration in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper with a parallel reimplementation of the disconnect flow (trpc.viewer.credentials.delete + its own invalidation set and toasts), rather than extending the existing component — changing the accepted disconnect UX (labeled trash button → ellipsis dropdown menu) as an unstated side effect of adding cache actions. Two independent implementations of app disconnection now exist and have already drifted: this one has no isPending/disabled state, so double-activating the confirm button fires the delete mutation twice, and its invalidation set (connectedCalendars + integrations) need not match DisconnectIntegration's; the next behavioral change to disconnection must be found and applied in both places or users of the two surfaces diverge.

[BUG] The handler throws a plain `Error("Credential not found or access denied")` for a caller-supplied credentialId that does not belong to the user, which tRPC surfaces as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) instead of a 4xx client error. Any stale or forged credentialId from the client produces a 500 with the message leaked to/logs as a server fault rather than NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN; the failure is a normal authorization rejection but is classified as a server crash, polluting error monitoring and breaking clients that branch on error codes.

[ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` inside a component that otherwise routes all copy through `useLocale()`, so the feature contradicts the app's localization intent. Every non-English-locale user sees the 'Last updated' timestamp rendered in en-US conventions (MM/DD/YYYY, 12-hour clock) while the surrounding label is in their own language — a regression against the i18n constraint the rest of the component honors, introduced without an explicit decision to exempt this string.

[BUG] TUNNEL_URL, extracted from third-party tunnelmole output via `grep -oE "$TM_KEYWORD"` (line 24), is interpolated unescaped into the sed replacement expression `s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|`, so sed metacharacters in the URL (`|` delimiter, `&` whole-match, `\1`-style backrefs) alter or break the substitution. A tunnelmole service (or MITM of its log output) returning a domain containing `|`, `&`, or backslash sequences corrupts the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL entry in .env or makes sed abort with an unterminated-command error, silently leaving a stale webhook URL configured; the shell quoting protects against shell-level injection but not sed-level injection.

[ADVISORY] The handler hard-instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` and always issues the `groupBy` query, bypassing the repository DI path that swaps in `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the calendar-cache feature is disabled — the mock's 'Skipping getCacheStatusByCredentialIds' path is dead code on this route. Every self-hosted deployment and environment with calendar-cache disabled pays one extra unconditional DB round-trip on every connectedCalendars fetch (a frequently called settings/onboarding endpoint), and the feature-disable switch silently does not cover this new query.

[ADVISORY] The not-found/ownership-failed path throws a plain `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`, which tRPC wraps as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than a 4xx the input contract implies. A user clicking delete on a credential that was concurrently disconnected (or a stale credentialId after refetch) gets a 500 on an expected 4xx condition, polluting error-rate monitoring with non-exceptions and hiding the intended message from the client in production; a TRPCError (NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN) is the correct shape.

[ADVISORY] `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, not the script location, so the sed/append block writes to whatever directory the script happens to be invoked from. A developer running `bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root gets `../.env` pointing at the repository's PARENT directory — the script creates and edits an unrelated .env outside the project (or fails confusingly), while the intended apps/.env is never updated, so the new webhook URL is silently not applied; a fully-qualified path derived from the script directory fixes it.

[BUG] The new cache-refresh signal calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with an empty Prisma update data object, which Prisma rejects with a PrismaClientValidationError (updateMany requires at least one field in `data`). Every Google Calendar availability fetch that reaches this line throws after the cache read/write completes, failing the calendar-sync path for all users; the intended SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bump never happens. Even in versions that tolerate the empty object, Prisma does not bump an @updatedAt field on an update with no changed fields, so the touch silently no-ops and the cache-status feature never reflects refreshes.

[ADVISORY] ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() backfills every pre-existing cache row with the migration execution timestamp, not the row's actual last-write time. On the first UI load after deploy, every existing Google credential shows 'Cache Status: Last updated: <deploy time>' even when the underlying cache rows are stale or already past expiresAt, and the destructive-looking 'Delete cached data' action is surfaced for caches that are in fact expired; the misleading timestamp persists until each credential's next real cache write overwrites it.

[ADVISORY] The updateManyByCredentialId touch runs unconditionally on every fetchAvailability call, including the cache-hit path where no fetch or cache write occurred. Every free-busy availability check now issues an extra UPDATE rewriting the updatedAt column on every SelectedCalendar row under the credential, adding write amplification and row-version churn on the hottest calendar path (availability checks happen per booking-page load and per slot scan) — previously served with zero DB writes on cache hits.

[BUG] deleteCacheHandler throws a plain `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` when the credential lookup fails, which tRPC wraps as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) instead of a 4xx NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN response. A user whose credentialId resolves to a team-owned credential (which has teamId, not userId, so findFirst returns null) or a stale/removed credential gets a 500-class failure with a generic 'Error deleting cache' toast and the real message stripped server-side in production; the server error log is polluted with an expected authorization miss as a 500, and the API contract reports an internal error for what is a client-side 4xx condition.

[ADVISORY] The new `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs unconditionally at the end of the cached-availability method — on every call, including the case where fresh cache was served and no Google fetch happened — turning a read path into a DB write path. Every availability check (booking page loads, availability lookups) for a Google Calendar credential now issues an UPDATE touching all SelectedCalendar rows for that credential even when nothing was refreshed, adding per-request write load and row-lock churn proportional to calendar count; if this updateMany throws (transient DB failure), the whole availability read fails with a 500 even though valid cached availability was already in hand — a write-side failure now breaks a previously read-only operation.

[ADVISORY] The handler instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through the feature-flag-based repository selection whose disabled variant (CalendarCacheRepositoryMock, which exists in this diff and logs 'Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled') exists precisely for the flag-off case. When the calendar-cache feature flag is disabled, connectedCalendars still executes a real groupBy query against the CalendarCache table on every fetch, and rows left over from before the flag was turned off surface a live 'Cache Status / Delete cached data' UI for a feature that is disabled — the mock's disabled contract (return []) is silently bypassed on this endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new cache-refresh signal calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with an empty Prisma update data object, which Prisma rejects with a PrismaClientValidationError (updateMany requires at least one field in `data`). Every Google Calendar availability fetch that reaches this line throws after the cache read/write completes, failing the calendar-sync path for all users; the intended SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bump never happens. Even in versions that tolerate the empty object, Prisma does not bump an @updatedAt field on an update with no changed fields, so the touch silently no-ops and the cache-status feature never reflects refreshes.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new “refresh signal” calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`. The repository implementation (`packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts`) directly passes this `data` object to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`. An empty `data` update is invalid for Prisma `updateMany` (no fields to update), and even if it were accepted it would not change any fields, so it would not reliably bump `updatedAt` for `SelectedCalendar` as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() backfills every pre-existing cache row with the migration execution timestamp, not the row's actual last-write time. On the first UI load after deploy, every existing Google credential shows 'Cache Status: Last updated: <deploy time>' even when the underlying cache rows are stale or already past expiresAt, and the destructive-looking 'Delete cached data' action is surfaced for caches that are in fact expired; the misleading timestamp persists until each credential's next real cache write overwrites it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CalendarCache.updatedAt` as `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` in the migration and `@default(now()) @updatedAt` in the Prisma model. `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` then derives `cacheUpdatedAt` from `MAX(updatedAt)` per credential and `CredentialActionsDropdown` treats any non-null `cacheUpdatedAt` as “has cache” and displays “Last updated: {{timestamp}}” plus the destructive “Delete cached data” action without checking `expiresAt`. For pre-existing `CalendarCache` rows, the added column will be populated with the migration execution time (via the default), so the UI will misleadingly show deploy time as the last update and surface the delete action even for expired/stale cache rows until a real cache write updates `updatedAt`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The updateManyByCredentialId touch runs unconditionally on every fetchAvailability call, including the cache-hit path where no fetch or cache write occurred. Every free-busy availability check now issues an extra UPDATE rewriting the updatedAt column on every SelectedCalendar row under the credential, adding write amplification and row-version churn on the hottest calendar path (availability checks happen per booking-page load and per slot scan) — previously served with zero DB writes on cache hits.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` is placed unconditionally after the cache/fetch block (i.e., outside the `if` that wraps `fetchAvailability`/`setAvailabilityInCache`). That means every invocation of this method will execute a DB `updateMany` against all `SelectedCalendar` rows for the credential, even when the earlier block doesn’t run (e.g., cache-hit paths), creating extra write load on a hot availability path. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the diff rather than a direct functional defect proven here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteCacheHandler throws a plain `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` when the credential lookup fails, which tRPC wraps as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) instead of a 4xx NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN response. A user whose credentialId resolves to a team-owned credential (which has teamId, not userId, so findFirst returns null) or a stale/removed credential gets a 500-class failure with a generic 'Error deleting cache' toast and the real message stripped server-side in production; the server error log is polluted with an expected authorization miss as a 500, and the API contract reports an internal error for what is a client-side 4xx condition.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler does `findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })` and, when not found, throws a plain `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. The diff does not show any `TRPCError` usage or error mapping, so this will be treated by tRPC as an internal server error rather than a 4xx-style NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN. The client side (`CredentialActionsDropdown`) also shows a generic toast on `onError`, so expected auth misses/stale IDs become 500-class failures with little feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs unconditionally at the end of the cached-availability method — on every call, including the case where fresh cache was served and no Google fetch happened — turning a read path into a DB write path. Every availability check (booking page loads, availability lookups) for a Google Calendar credential now issues an UPDATE touching all SelectedCalendar rows for that credential even when nothing was refreshed, adding per-request write load and row-lock churn proportional to calendar count; if this updateMany throws (transient DB failure), the whole availability read fails with a 500 even though valid cached availability was already in hand — a write-side failure now breaks a previously read-only operation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the added `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` is placed outside the preceding conditional block that fetches and writes availability into the cache, so it will execute every time this method runs, regardless of whether a Google fetch/cache refresh occurred. This introduces an unconditional DB write (`updateMany`) on a path that otherwise appears to be an availability read/cache-check flow, and there is no error isolation (no try/catch), meaning a failure in this extra write would propagate and fail the whole method call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through the feature-flag-based repository selection whose disabled variant (CalendarCacheRepositoryMock, which exists in this diff and logs 'Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled') exists precisely for the flag-off case. When the calendar-cache feature flag is disabled, connectedCalendars still executes a real groupBy query against the CalendarCache table on every fetch, and rows left over from before the flag was turned off surface a live 'Cache Status / Delete cached data' UI for a feature that is disabled — the mock's disabled contract (return []) is silently bypassed on this endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the diff unconditionally imports and instantiates the concrete `CalendarCacheRepository` (`const cacheRepository = new CalendarCacheRepository();`) and calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, which in `calendar-cache.repository.ts` performs a real `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy` query. The diff also updates `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` to implement the same method by returning `[]` and logging “Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled”, implying there is (elsewhere) a disabled/flag-off pathway intended to avoid DB work. This handler bypasses any such selection mechanism and hard-codes the real repository, which is a concrete, diff-grounded architectural/feature-flag consistency issue, though the existence/behavior of the flag-selection wiring itself is not shown in this diff.
